The applicant's full name, email address and phone number
The business name, location and LGA information requested in the online business application
For full business KYC, CAC/registration documents, BVN, valid ID, signature, passport photograph and Tax Identification Number
For a company account, board resolution, company references and SCUML certificate when the business activity requires SCUML registration
steps: Open FCMB's official business-account page and enter the company RC number for validation.
Enter the applicant's name, email, phone number, business location, LGA and registered business name.
Submit the initial application so FCMB can continue the business-account onboarding.
Prepare and provide the CAC, BVN, ID, signature, photograph, TIN and company-specific documents used for full KYC.
Confirm the approved business-account number and current operating-balance/fee terms before beginning normal business transactions.
notes: FCMB separates its personal online savings-account portal from the business online account route.
Company applicants can require additional documents such as board resolution, references and SCUML evidence.
Promotional free-banking periods and other benefits should be treated as current offers rather than permanent account rules.

title: How to open an ALAT account by Wema Bank
summary: ALAT by Wema's fully digital account-opening route using the mobile app, phone verification, identity details, selfie and BVN for full features without a branch visit.
feeLabel: Free digital account opening
feeNote: ALAT presents account opening as free. Normal transaction, card or other product charges can apply after the account is active.
timeline: ALAT states that a digital account can be opened in minutes after the signup and identity checks are completed.
requirements: A smartphone capable of installing the ALAT app
A Nigerian phone number that can receive the verification code
A valid identity document for digital onboarding
A BVN for the full-feature account route, although ALAT's FAQ says some signup access can begin without BVN
A selfie/facial capture used by ALAT to confirm the customer's identity
steps: Download the official ALAT app from the Play Store or App Store link shown on ALAT's website and choose Open an Account.
Enter the phone number and submit the verification code sent to the device.
Enter the customer's identity/profile information and BVN for the full-feature account setup.
Complete the selfie/facial-identity check and create a secure password for the new profile.
Confirm the new account in the ALAT dashboard and review the account limits before making higher-value transactions.
notes: ALAT says the account-opening process is fully digital and does not require a branch visit.
The current FAQ says BVN is optional for initial signup but recommended for full features, while the main onboarding page shows BVN as part of identity confirmation.
Use only the official ALAT app because credentials, OTPs and passwords should never be shared with an agent.

title: How to request and activate an ALAT debit card
summary: ALAT's in-app debit-card route for choosing a card design, confirming with the ALAT PIN, entering a delivery address and activating the delivered card from the app.
feeLabel: Card charge shown in the ALAT app
feeNote: ALAT's public card page describes the request and delivery workflow but does not publish one durable universal card price. Confirm the current card and delivery amount in the app before submitting the request.
timeline: ALAT's current card page states that requested cards are delivered within 72 hours, subject to the delivery information and provider operations.
requirements: An active ALAT account with access to the mobile app
The ALAT PIN needed to confirm the debit-card request
A valid Nigerian delivery address for the physical card
The delivered card details used by the app during activation
steps: Sign in to the ALAT app and open the Cards section.
Swipe through the available card designs and choose the preferred debit card.
Confirm the request with the ALAT PIN, enter the delivery address and submit the card order.
After the card arrives, sign in to ALAT and choose Activate New Card.
Enter the delivered card information requested by the app and complete activation before using the card at an ATM, online or in stores.
notes: ALAT states that physical card delivery is available nationwide in Nigeria.
The app also provides controls to freeze, block or limit card spending.
A virtual/dollar card is a different ALAT product from the physical debit-card delivery workflow.

title: How to open a Sterling account with OneBank
summary: Sterling Bank's OneBank onboarding route for new customers using BVN, name and date of birth to create a Tier 1 account, or for existing Sterling customers validating an existing account.
feeLabel: OneBank app use is free; transaction charges can apply
feeNote: Sterling states that using the OneBank application is free. Charges can apply when the customer performs chargeable banking transactions.
timeline: Sterling says customers can open an account in minutes; the initial Tier 1 or wallet account becomes available after successful onboarding and validation.
requirements: For a new Sterling customer, a BVN plus the customer's name and date of birth
Access to the phone number and email associated with the BVN so the OTP can be received
For an existing Sterling customer, the account number plus OTP, card or USSD validation
A username/login credential and transaction PIN created during registration
steps: Download the official Sterling OneBank app and start registration as an existing Sterling customer or a new customer.
For a new customer, enter the BVN, name and date of birth and submit the OTP sent to the BVN-linked phone/email.
For an existing customer, enter the Sterling account number and complete OTP, card or USSD validation.
Create the OneBank login credentials and transaction PIN after successful validation.
Sign in and complete the security-question setup, then check whether the profile shows a wallet/Tier 1 account or a fully upgraded account.
notes: Sterling's current FAQ says a new non-customer is initially given a Tier 1 account after BVN onboarding.
The OneBank app can also expose existing Sterling accounts for an already banked customer.
Higher transaction limits require the account to be upgraded beyond the basic wallet/Tier 1 level.

title: How to upgrade a Sterling OneBank wallet or Tier 1 account
summary: Sterling OneBank's self-service upgrade route using BVN validation, facial verification, identity documents, e-signature and residential-address verification to convert a wallet/Tier 1 account to a full account.
feeLabel: No OneBank account-upgrade fee stated
feeNote: Sterling's FAQ does not state a separate fee for the self-service KYC upgrade from wallet/Tier 1 to a full account.
timeline: Sterling does not publish one fixed completion time for every KYC upgrade; the app submits the identity and address checks during the self-service flow.
requirements: An existing OneBank wallet or Tier 1 account
A BVN for the full-account upgrade
A well-lit selfie for facial verification
A valid ID number and clear ID-card image; Sterling's FAQ also describes NIN/Virtual NIN handling
A signature specimen and current residential address for address verification
steps: Sign in to OneBank and tap the Upgrade option on the wallet or Tier 1 account shown on the dashboard.
Choose the preferred full account type and enter the employment information shown by OneBank.
Provide and validate the BVN, then complete the well-lit selfie/facial-verification step.
Choose the ID type, enter the ID number and upload the ID image plus signature specimen.
Enter the residential address, submit the verification and confirm that OneBank now displays the upgraded full-account status and limits.
notes: Sterling's FAQ says a full-KYC OneBank account can have materially higher transaction limits than a wallet account.
Address verification can use OneBank's location/address-verification service, so the customer should enter a current residential address.
A failed facial validation does not mean the customer should send identity documents to an unofficial support contact.

title: How to buy a Hygeia HMO health plan
summary: Hygeia HMO's online purchase route for individuals, families and SMEs: compare current health plans, choose Get Started or Subscribe, enter enrollee details, pay and receive registration confirmation.
feeLabel: Price depends on the selected Hygeia plan and payment period
feeNote: Hygeia publishes current plan prices and promotional discounts on its live plan pages. Confirm the final plan, payment frequency, waiting period and amount immediately before purchase because pricing can change.
timeline: Hygeia says the customer receives an automated response when registration is complete and its team then follows up through the registered email address or phone number.
requirements: A selected Hygeia individual, family or SME health plan that matches the enrolment type
The enrollee's identity and contact information entered during the subscription
Dependent information for a family or multi-person plan
A supported online payment method for the plan price shown during checkout
steps: Open Hygeia HMO's official Plan List and compare the plan type, provider category, benefits, limits, waiting periods and current price.
Choose Get Started or Subscribe on the selected plan and enter the enrollee information.
Add the required dependent or additional-member information when purchasing a family or multi-person plan.
Review the selected plan and current payment amount, then complete the online payment.
Save the automated registration confirmation and monitor the registered email/phone for Hygeia's next enrolment and access information.
notes: This guide explains the provider's purchase process and does not recommend which health plan is medically or financially suitable for a particular person.
Hygeia plans differ in hospital categories, benefit limits, waiting periods and covered services; read the selected plan's visible benefits before paying.
Current website promotional discounts can change and should not be treated as permanent annual prices.

title: How to find a Hygeia HMO hospital or provider
summary: Hygeia HMO's provider-directory route for searching hospitals, clinics, dental providers, pharmacies and other network facilities by name, category, coverage, city or state.
feeLabel: No provider-directory search fee
feeNote: Hygeia provides the provider-directory search without a separate search charge; access to a specific facility or service still depends on the member's active plan and benefit rules.
timeline: The online directory returns matching network providers immediately after the customer searches or filters the provider table.
requirements: The member's Hygeia plan/provider category when the customer wants to limit results to facilities covered by the plan
A location such as state, city or town when searching for nearby network facilities
An optional hospital/provider name or coverage type such as medical, dental or pharmacy
steps: Open Hygeia HMO's official Provider Directory.
Enter a provider name or use the category, coverage, city, address or state filters to narrow the network.
Review the provider category and coverage type against the member's active Hygeia plan.
Open or note the selected provider's address and location information before travelling.
Confirm plan eligibility or pre-authorisation with Hygeia when the intended treatment requires approval beyond simply locating a network provider.
notes: Hygeia's directory labels providers by network category, and higher-premium provider categories may not be available on every plan.
A facility appearing in the directory does not mean every treatment at that facility is covered by every Hygeia plan.
For urgent medical care, use appropriate emergency services rather than delaying treatment to browse a directory.

title: How to pay a PHED bill or buy a prepaid token
summary: PHED's online payment route for entering a prepaid meter or customer record, choosing an amount and payment method, then receiving the electricity token and transaction receipt.
feeLabel: Electricity amount plus any payment-channel charge
feeNote: The electricity amount depends on the customer's meter/account and tariff. PHED's payment portal shows the transaction amount before the customer confirms card, transfer, USSD or mobile-money payment.
timeline: PHED's current payment portal says prepaid tokens are generated instantly after successful payment and customers should contact support if the token is not received within five minutes.
requirements: The PHED prepaid meter number or customer/account information used by the payment portal
The amount the customer intends to pay or use to purchase electricity
A phone number or email address for receiving the transaction receipt or token information
A supported card, bank-transfer, USSD or mobile-money payment method
steps: Open PHED's official payment portal and enter the meter/account and customer contact information.
Enter the electricity amount and confirm that the customer or meter record is the intended one.
Choose card, bank transfer, USSD or another payment method offered by PHED and complete the transaction.
Save the generated receipt and copy the 20-digit electricity token for a prepaid meter.
If the token is not displayed or received within five minutes, use PHED's token requery/support route with the transaction reference.
notes: PHED's portal states that Visa, Mastercard, Verve, bank transfer, USSD and mobile-money options are supported.
The payment portal includes a token-check/requery route for a successful transaction whose token did not arrive normally.
Always verify the meter number before payment because the generated token is linked to that prepaid meter.

title: How to apply for a PHED prepaid meter under MAP
summary: PHED's online MAP meter route for entering customer, premises, ID and meter details, resolving existing arrears, receiving approval and paying securely through the approved meter application portal.
feeLabel: Meter price depends on approved vendor and meter type
feeNote: PHED's live MAP portal publishes approved vendor pricing. Use the price and transaction reference displayed for the approved application rather than an older tariff or a field-agent quote.
timeline: PHED provides live application tracking but does not publish one universal installation completion time for every MAP application on the current portal.
requirements: The customer's name, occupation, phone number and email address
The service address including state, LGA, house number, bus stop and landmark
The PHED account number, existing meter information if any, and a valid ID type/number
The required meter type and accepted MAP payment option selected in the application
Resolution of existing account arrears through payoff, an accepted installment arrangement or PHED's bill-revision route before approved payment
steps: Open PHED's official MAP portal and start a prepaid-meter application for the customer account.
Enter the customer, premises, account, ID and requested-meter information and submit the meter request.
Resolve any account arrears by paying them, accepting the installment option PHED offers or opening a bill-revision request if the balance is disputed.
Wait until PHED marks the application approved for payment, then use the displayed transaction reference and portal payment route to pay the approved meter amount.
Keep the ticket ID/payment evidence and use PHED's portal to track the meter application through installation.
notes: PHED's MAP form says the customer must address arrears before completing a meter purchase.
The current MAP portal publishes approved Meter Asset Provider pricing and supports status tracking and secure payment.
Customers should quote the PHED ticket ID on transactions connected to the meter application.

title: How to pay a Kaduna Electric bill or buy a prepaid token
summary: Kaduna Electric's official and authorised e-payment routes for entering a prepaid meter or postpaid account, completing payment and receiving the STS token or transaction receipt.
feeLabel: Electricity amount plus any payment-channel charge
feeNote: The electricity amount depends on the customer's tariff and purchase. Kaduna Electric lists its direct portal plus authorised banks, fintechs, POS and USSD channels; review the channel checkout before payment.
timeline: Kaduna Electric states that its authorised digital vending channels generate prepaid STS tokens instantly after successful payment.
requirements: The 11-digit or 13-digit prepaid meter number or the postpaid account reference
The amount the customer wants to vend or pay toward the monthly electricity bill
A supported payment option such as debit card, bank transfer, mobile wallet, USSD or an authorised cashier/POS route
A phone number or email address for the token/transaction notification on digital channels
steps: Open Kaduna Electric's official e-payment page or direct customer portal and choose an authorised digital or walk-in payment channel.
Enter the prepaid meter number or postpaid account reference and confirm the customer record.
Enter the electricity amount and complete checkout with the selected card, transfer, mobile-wallet, USSD or cash channel.
For a prepaid meter, copy the 20-digit STS token displayed and sent after successful vending.
Keep the receipt and contact Kaduna Electric support if the token does not load after the meter/UIU pairing and activation checks are satisfied.
notes: Kaduna Electric publishes authorised payment partners and physical cashier/service locations across Kaduna, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara.
Its digital-vending guide says the STS token is returned on-screen and through SMS/email after successful payment.
A token-loading problem can be caused by UIU pairing or activation rather than the payment itself.

title: How to apply for a Kaduna Electric prepaid meter under MAP
summary: Kaduna Electric's current five-stage MAP route: submit the meter request, pass the premises survey, resolve outstanding debt, pay the approved provider and receive installation after payment confirmation.
feeLabel: Current MAP price depends on provider and meter type
feeNote: Kaduna Electric publishes a live provider-by-provider MAP price table. Pay only the current regulated amount shown for the selected single- or three-phase meter and approved MAP provider.
timeline: Kaduna Electric states that after MAP payment is confirmed and the site passes inspection, the meter is installed and energised within 10 working days.
requirements: An existing Kaduna Electric account/meter reference for an existing customer, or completion of new-customer enrolment before MAP selection
Customer/account details, valid ID and property information used for the online meter request
A premises that passes the pre-installation wiring/load and meter-type survey
Settlement of outstanding electricity debt or an approved flexible repayment arrangement
Payment directly into the designated account of the approved MAP provider after eligibility and meter type are confirmed
steps: Open Kaduna Electric's MAP eligibility portal and enter the account or meter number, or complete new-customer enrolment at the area office first.
Submit the online meter request with the customer, valid-ID and property information.
Allow Kaduna Electric/MAP inspectors to assess the premises and determine the required single- or three-phase meter.
Clear outstanding electricity debt or agree the approved repayment plan, then pay the current MAP amount directly to the designated provider account and upload the receipt.
Track the request and allow the licensed technicians to install and energise the smart meter within the published 10-working-day post-payment window.
notes: Kaduna Electric tells new buildings, first-time customers and account-separation applicants to complete area-office enrolment before meter payment.
The provider warns customers not to pay cash to field technicians or unverified third parties.
Current MAP prices vary by provider, communication technology and meter phase, so the live MAP price table should be checked immediately before payment.

sources.label: Kaduna Electric New Customer Connection & Metering

title: How to replace or swap an MTN SIM in Nigeria
summary: MTN Nigeria's SIM swap/replacement route for a lost, stolen, damaged, faulty or obsolete line, using the registered number, NIN/VNIN and ownership/usage verification before the old number is moved to a new SIM.
feeLabel: New replacement SIM cost applies
feeNote: MTN states that the customer purchases a new SIM card for the swap; the current replacement-SIM price is determined by MTN and should be confirmed at the MTN outlet before payment.
timeline: MTN does not publish one fixed completion time for every SIM swap; completion depends on identity, NIN and line-ownership verification.
requirements: An MTN phone number that is already registered
The customer's National Identification Number or Virtual NIN
Correct line-usage information when MTN asks for ownership checks, such as last recharge amount/date, frequently dialled numbers and year of activation
A new MTN SIM card onto which the existing phone number can be transferred
steps: Open MTN Nigeria's SIM Swap page or visit an MTN store and request replacement of the registered line.
Provide the registered phone number and NIN or Virtual NIN for identity validation.
Answer the line-ownership questions MTN presents, including usage information when those checks appear.
Purchase the replacement MTN SIM and allow the MTN agent or approved swap channel to transfer the existing number to it.
Confirm that the replacement SIM registers on the MTN network and test calls/SMS before discarding the old or damaged SIM.
notes: MTN lists lost, stolen, damaged, faulty and obsolete SIMs as reasons a customer may need a swap or replacement.
A SIM swap keeps the existing phone number but replaces the physical SIM profile.
For a stolen phone or SIM, report the loss promptly and do not disclose OTPs or banking credentials to anyone offering an unofficial swap.

title: How to port your phone number to MTN in Nigeria
summary: MTN Nigeria's Mobile Number Portability route for switching from another Nigerian network to MTN while retaining the same number, with online/3232 validation, valid ID and in-person biometric completion.
feeLabel: Free porting
feeNote: MTN states that the online request and PORT/3232 validation are free.
timeline: MTN says the porting process normally takes about 15–20 minutes after initiation and can take up to 48 hours.
requirements: An active Nigerian mobile number currently on another network
A line that has not been ported during the previous 45 days
A valid regulatory ID such as driver's licence, voter card or National ID
Personal attendance at an MTN outlet for biometric and SIM-registration completion
steps: Open MTN's official Mobile Number Portability page and submit the Port Now request with the mobile-number details.
Send PORT by SMS to 3232 or dial 3232 and complete the IVR validation from the number being ported.
Back up SIM contacts and use or withdraw any remaining airtime/mobile-money value that would be lost after porting.
Visit an MTN outlet with the current phone number and valid ID and complete the required biometric/SIM registration.
Wait for MTN's status messages and insert/use the new MTN SIM after the port is confirmed complete.
notes: MTN says the subscriber cannot port again until 45 days after the most recent port.
Unused airtime, voicemail, SMS settings and subscriptions from the former operator do not transfer to MTN.
A proxy cannot complete the biometric stage for the subscriber.

title: How to upgrade or swap an Airtel SIM to 4G
summary: Airtel Nigeria's route for moving an existing number to a 4G-compatible USIM through an Airtel shop/partner outlet or the available self-service SIM swap, while retaining the phone number.
feeLabel: Current Airtel SIM cost applies
feeNote: Airtel states that the current SIM cost applies to a 4G LTE SIM swap; confirm the amount at the Airtel outlet or self-service route before completing the swap.
timeline: Airtel does not publish one universal completion time for every 4G SIM swap; the number is retained after the swap is completed.
requirements: An existing Airtel line that needs a 4G-compatible SIM/USIM
A 4G-compatible phone or device if the customer intends to use Airtel LTE service
The identity/SIM-swap documents requested by Airtel for ownership verification
A replacement Airtel SIM obtained through an Airtel shop, partner outlet or supported self-service swap
steps: Open Airtel Nigeria's 4G support page and confirm that the existing SIM needs an upgrade for 4G/LTE service.
Visit an Airtel shop or partner outlet, or start Airtel's supported self-service SIM swap route.
Complete Airtel's ownership and identity verification for the existing mobile number.
Pay the current replacement-SIM amount and complete the swap from the old SIM to the new 4G-capable Airtel SIM.
Insert/activate the new SIM, enable LTE/4G in the device network settings and confirm that the existing Airtel number remains active.
notes: Airtel says the customer's existing phone number is retained after the 4G SIM swap.
A special 4G data plan is not required; eligible Airtel data plans can work across 2G/3G/4G.
The 4G SIM upgrade is different from Airtel eSIM activation.

title: How to replace a lost or stolen Glo SIM
summary: Globacom's SIM replacement route at a Gloworld shop using valid ID and line-ownership evidence, with separate supporting documents for prepaid and Glo Business customers.
feeLabel: ₦100 SIM replacement fee
feeNote: Glo's current Self Care page lists a ₦100 SIM replacement cost.
timeline: Glo does not publish one fixed completion time for every physical SIM replacement; processing depends on identity and ownership verification at the Gloworld shop.
requirements: The original and a photocopy of a valid photo ID such as National ID, driver's licence or international passport
For a prepaid line, the SIM certificate/cardholder or purchase receipt plus a police report and sworn affidavit
For a Glo Business line, the SIM certificate, service/application evidence, recent invoices and corporate introduction plus a police report and sworn affidavit
A visit to a Gloworld shop handling SIM replacement
steps: Open Glo's Self Care page and identify the nearest Gloworld shop that handles SIM replacement.
Prepare the original and photocopy of the valid photo ID and the ownership documents matching prepaid or Glo Business service.
Prepare the police report and sworn affidavit listed by Glo for the lost/stolen replacement route.
Visit the Gloworld shop, submit the replacement form and ownership evidence and pay the current ₦100 replacement charge.
Confirm that the old number is active on the replacement SIM before leaving the service location.
notes: Glo provides separate replacement forms for prepaid, Glo Business and proxy replacement scenarios.
The provider's published ID list includes National ID, driver's licence, international passport and other photo-bearing categories.
A lost/stolen SIM should be secured promptly because control of the mobile number can affect banking and other OTP-based services.

title: How to port your phone number to Glo
summary: Glo's Mobile Number Portability route for switching an existing prepaid or postpaid Nigerian number to Glo, free of charge, with in-person identity verification and a new Glo SIM.
feeLabel: Free porting
feeNote: Glo states that Mobile Number Portability is free.
timeline: Glo states that the porting process takes a maximum of 48 hours.
requirements: An existing prepaid or postpaid Nigerian mobile number on another network
A valid identity document such as National ID, passport, driver's licence or another officially validated photo ID
NIN when the subscriber cannot present an accepted identity card
An in-person visit to a Gloworld shop or authorised Glo dealer because Glo says porting cannot be completed by phone or online
steps: Open Glo's official Mobile Number Portability page and review the eligibility and porting conditions.
Use any remaining airtime or service value on the old network because Glo states that outstanding credit is forfeited on porting.
Visit a Gloworld shop or authorised Glo dealer with the number and valid ID or NIN.
Complete the Glo port-in and identity/SIM-registration process and receive the new Glo SIM linked to the existing number.
Wait for the porting-status SMS messages and begin using the Glo SIM after the port is confirmed.
notes: Glo says a subscriber must wait 45 days after a port before porting the number again.
Porting does not transfer the former network's tariff, subscriptions, voicemail or other ancillary services.
The subscriber can cancel only before the confirmation stage; after confirmation the port proceeds to completion.

title: How to use Glo international roaming
summary: Glo's international roaming route for prepaid and postpaid customers, including default prepaid roaming, postpaid activation before travel, partner-network selection and balance/recharge handling abroad.
feeLabel: Prepaid: no activation fee; Postpaid: ₦50,000 subscription fee
feeNote: Glo's current roaming page states that prepaid roaming is enabled by default with no extra registration/subscription charge, while postpaid roaming requires a ₦50,000 subscription fee 2–3 days before travel. Roaming usage rates vary by country/network.
timeline: Prepaid roaming is already enabled on eligible lines; Glo tells postpaid customers to activate roaming 2–3 days before travel.
requirements: A Glo prepaid or postpaid line and a compatible handset for the destination's mobile-network frequencies
Enough prepaid airtime before travel, or completed postpaid roaming activation before departure
A destination with an active Glo roaming-partner network
Network selection on the handset when automatic registration does not choose the required partner
steps: Open Glo's roaming page and check that the destination has a supported roaming partner and that the handset supports the local network frequencies.
For prepaid service, load enough airtime before travel; for postpaid service, visit a Gloworld outlet and activate roaming/pay the current subscription 2–3 days before departure.
On arrival, switch on the phone and allow automatic network selection to register the line on a roaming partner.
If automatic registration fails, open the phone's network-selection settings and manually choose a supported Glo roaming partner.
Monitor airtime/usage while abroad and use Glo's roaming customer-care route if the line cannot register or make supported calls.
notes: Glo's prepaid roaming service is enabled by default but is available only in supported partner countries/networks.
International roaming rates vary with country, partner and exchange-rate changes and should be checked before travel.
Glo recommends travelling with a 4G-compatible SIM because some partner networks have shut down older 2G/3G services.

title: How to buy a Glo data roaming bundle
summary: Glo's data-roaming bundle route through *312# option 5, with bundle activation at the roaming destination and a requirement to use supported partner networks to avoid ordinary pay-as-you-go roaming rates.
feeLabel: Current bundles range from ₦2,500 to ₦50,000
feeNote: Glo's current data-roaming page lists bundles from ₦2,500 to ₦50,000 with different data allowances and validity periods. Confirm the *312# menu before purchase because bundle prices and partner networks can change.
timeline: Glo states that the data-roaming bundle activates when the subscriber lands at the roaming destination and begins browsing on a supported network.
requirements: An active Glo line with international roaming available for the account type
Enough account balance to purchase the selected data-roaming bundle
A destination and partner network included in Glo's current supported roaming-bundle list
For a postpaid customer, international roaming activation before subscribing to the data-roaming bundle
steps: Open Glo's current Data Roaming page and check that the destination/partner network supports the roaming bundle.
Dial *312# from the Glo line and select option 5 for Data Roaming Bundles.
Choose the bundle with the required allowance, price and validity and confirm the purchase.
On arrival at the destination, connect the phone to one of Glo's recommended partner networks.
Begin using mobile data and check the bundle balance/validity so the line does not fall back to ordinary pay-as-you-go roaming unexpectedly.
notes: Glo says a roaming bundle can also be purchased while the customer is already abroad.
Using a network outside the supported bundle partner list can cause pay-as-you-go roaming charges.
Prepaid roaming is enabled by default, but a postpaid customer needs roaming activation before buying the data bundle.

title: How to pay an EEDC electricity bill online
summary: EEDC's payment route through EnergyPay and other approved channels for prepaid and postpaid customers, with customer/account verification and an electronic receipt after successful payment.
feeLabel: Electricity amount plus any channel charge
feeNote: EEDC states that debit-card payment through its online route does not attract an extra EEDC charge, while some mobile/POS/other channels can charge a transaction fee. Confirm the selected channel before payment.
timeline: EEDC issues an electronic receipt after successful online payment; it does not publish one universal crediting time for every approved payment channel.
requirements: The EEDC customer/account or prepaid meter information used to identify the electricity service
The amount the customer intends to pay or vend
A supported debit card, bank, payment-agent, ATM or other EEDC-listed payment channel
Access to the electronic receipt after a successful transaction
steps: Open EEDC's official website and choose Make Payment or the EnergyPay payment option.
Enter the customer account or prepaid meter information and verify the returned electricity record before continuing.
Enter the payment amount and choose an available approved payment channel.
Complete the payment and save the electronic receipt issued as evidence of the transaction.
If the payment does not reflect on the customer account, contact EEDC with the account details and electronic receipt for reconciliation.
notes: EEDC lists online payment, banks, collection agents, ATM and other electronic routes on its current payment guidance.
The provider says customers should insist on an electronic receipt because it is evidence of payment.
A payment-status or billing problem should be raised with EEDC using the receipt rather than paying the same bill again immediately.

title: How to use EEDC Connect for bills and complaints
summary: EEDC's mobile self-service route for registering with OTP, paying bills, viewing payment history, lodging support requests and tracking complaints without visiting a district office.
feeLabel: No EEDC Connect registration fee stated
feeNote: EEDC does not state a separate charge for registering the self-service app; electricity payments made through supported payment channels remain subject to their normal terms.
timeline: Registration is completed after the OTP is validated. Complaint and support resolution times depend on the issue logged with EEDC.
requirements: A smartphone that can install the EEDC Connect mobile application
A customer phone number capable of receiving the registration OTP
The EEDC customer/account information needed to link electricity services in the app
Complaint or payment details when the customer uses the support and history features
steps: Download EEDC Connect from the app-store route published by EEDC and open the application.
Register the customer profile and request the one-time password sent to the supplied mobile number.
Enter the OTP sent to the registered phone number, then add the EEDC account number shown on the customer's electricity bill so the app can display that service record.
Use the app to pay bills, view payment history or submit a customer-support complaint.
Open the logged complaint or payment history later to check the status and retain the reference until the issue is resolved.
notes: EEDC describes the app as a self-service platform for bill payment, support, payment history and complaint tracking.
The app does not replace emergency safety reporting for dangerous electrical faults.
EEDC also operates other self-service channels such as EEDC BOT and its website.

title: How to apply for a new EEDC electricity connection
summary: EEDC's new-service application route for a premises needing electricity supply, using the customer/service form, identity and premises information, load details, preferred billing/payment information and technical clearance.

feeNote: EEDC does not publish one flat new-connection charge for every premises because the technical load, service work and metering needs can differ. Obtain the official assessed amount before payment.
timeline: EEDC does not publish one universal completion time for all new-service connections; the application moves through commercial, metering, credit-control and final approval checks.
requirements: The applicant's identity, phone/contact and current or previous residential information
The full address of the premises requiring electricity supply, including premises type and intended use
A valid means of identification such as an international passport, driver's licence or PVC
The requested electrical load/service information and property planning/earthing information shown on EEDC's new-service form
steps: Open EEDC's official Customer Information area and obtain the current New Service Form.
Complete the applicant identity, contact, premises address, premises type and intended electricity-use sections.
Provide the valid ID details and the electrical/load information needed for the proposed connection.
Submit the form to EEDC so the commercial, metering and credit-control sections can assess and clear the application.
Pay only the official assessed connection amount after EEDC approval and keep the receipt and final connection/account information.
notes: EEDC's new-service form also supports some changes such as additional load, change of customer and additional meter, but those tasks can require separate assessment.
A new connection can require technical work beyond simply creating a billing account.
Customers should not pay an unofficial contractor before EEDC has assessed and approved the service.

title: How to apply for a KEDCO prepaid meter under MAP

A completed KEDCO MAP meter application form or online application
The customer and premises information used by KEDCO to determine the appropriate single- or three-phase meter
Payment only after the approved MAP provider and current official meter amount have been confirmed
steps: Open KEDCO's official MAP meter page and start the online application or download the meter form.
Complete the customer/account, premises and contact information required for the meter request.
Submit the request through KEDCO or take the completed form to the nearest KEDCO office as the provider directs.
Confirm the assigned MAP provider, meter phase and current official amount before making payment.
Keep the application and payment evidence and follow up with KEDCO for provider assignment, site work and meter installation.
notes: KEDCO's current MAP page names several approved Meter Asset Providers serving Kano, Katsina and Jigawa.
The meter-price figures displayed on the current KEDCO page appear internally inconsistent by phase, so this guide deliberately marks the fee as a conflict.
A meter should be acquired through KEDCO/MAP channels rather than an unapproved seller.

A registered electrical contractor to prepare and forward the connection application under KEDCO's published route
Technical information sufficient for KEDCO to assess whether the load can use a public transformer or needs a dedicated transformer
Any customer identity/property information requested during KEDCO's connection assessment
steps: Open KEDCO's official FAQ and confirm the new premises' expected electrical load with a registered electrical contractor.
Have the registered contractor prepare the new-connection application and required technical information for KEDCO.
Submit the application to KEDCO for load assessment and network-availability review.
Receive KEDCO's technical decision on the connection arrangement, including whether a public or dedicated transformer is needed.
Pay only the official assessed connection charges and keep the approval/account details after KEDCO authorises the new supply.
notes: KEDCO's current FAQ says loads below 50 KVA can be connected through a public transformer when capacity is available, while higher loads need a dedicated transformer.
Actual connection voltage and infrastructure depend on load capacity and available mains.
A registered electrical contractor's involvement does not replace KEDCO's final technical approval.

The amount the customer wants to vend or pay toward the electricity bill
Use of a payment channel that KEDCO currently lists as active for that customer/account
The transaction receipt or token information needed for any later complaint
steps: Open KEDCO's official website and check the current Buy Electricity Token or payment options shown for the customer.
Enter the prepaid meter or postpaid account reference only on the active KEDCO-authorised channel.
Confirm the customer record and amount before completing the transaction.
Save the receipt and, for a prepaid purchase, the generated STS token.
If the digital route is unavailable or contradicts the account's instructions, contact the nearest KEDCO office/customer care before making a second payment.
notes: KEDCO's current homepage advertises digital prepaid token and postpaid bill settlement.
KEDCO's FAQ still says bill payment is restricted to the customer's Business Unit/Sub-Business Unit and prepaid vending is available at KEDCO offices; this conflict is left visible.
Do not use an unofficial payment link merely because an older KEDCO FAQ appears restrictive.

title: How to file an insurance claim with Leadway

feeLabel: No claim-filing fee stated

A completed claim form or claim notification through Leadway's claim channel
Evidence of the loss such as photographs, repair estimates, receipts or other policy-specific supporting documents
For motor third-party injury/death claims, the police report or other documents listed by Leadway for the incident

Upload or submit the supporting evidence required for the policy, such as damage photographs, repair estimates and police report for applicable motor third-party claims.
Respond to any loss-adjustment or documentation request and review the claim offer/discharge voucher when Leadway completes assessment.
Sign/return the discharge voucher when the settlement is accepted and keep the payment/closure record after Leadway settles the approved claim.
notes: Leadway's third-party motor terms say accidents should be notified within 30 days and provide a claims-centre route.
Leadway publishes different target timelines for general insurance and life assurance claims.
This guide explains claim submission only; whether a loss is covered depends on the specific policy wording and claim facts.

title: How to block a Sterling account if your phone is lost
summary: Sterling Bank's emergency USSD account-block route using *822*911# from any mobile phone for registered Sterling USSD users when a device is lost or unauthorised access is suspected.
feeLabel: No emergency-block fee stated
feeNote: Sterling's OneBank FAQ does not state a separate charge for using the published *822*911# emergency block route.
timeline: Sterling presents *822*911# as an immediate emergency action; account recovery after blocking uses Sterling support or branch assistance.

Access to any mobile phone capable of dialing the *822*911# emergency code
The account-owner information requested by Sterling's USSD prompts
Official Sterling support details for follow-up if the account or OneBank profile must later be restored
steps: Open the phone dialler on any available mobile phone and dial *822*911# as soon as the Sterling account is at risk.
Complete the account-identification and security prompts shown by Sterling's emergency USSD menu.
Confirm the request to block the Sterling account from further unauthorised access.
Review recent activity through a safe official channel after the account is secured.
Contact Sterling's One Customer Centre or visit a branch for recovery/unblocking assistance after the threat has been contained.
notes: Sterling says the emergency code works for customers who are already registered Sterling USSD users.
A customer who has not registered for USSD can dial *822# and use Registration, but this should not delay other official fraud-reporting steps during an active compromise.
Sterling warns customers never to disclose OTPs or security credentials to callers or message senders.

title: How to pay a YEDC bill or buy prepaid electricity units

feeLabel: Electricity amount plus any channel charge
feeNote: The amount depends on the customer's bill, meter and tariff. YEDC says prepaid customers can buy units online from its website or at YEDC offices, while postpaid customers can pay through their Business Unit or Service Center.
timeline: Payment is applied after the selected channel confirms the transaction; YEDC does not publish one universal crediting time for every payment route.
requirements: The YEDC account number for a postpaid customer or prepaid meter number for a vending customer
The amount the customer wants to pay or use to purchase prepaid electricity units
Access to YEDC's online purchase route, Business Unit, Service Center or another provider-approved payment point
steps: Open YEDC's official website and choose the Buy Units or payment route, or use the relevant YEDC Business Unit or Service Center.
Enter or provide the customer account or prepaid meter number and confirm the returned customer information before paying.
Enter the intended payment amount and complete the transaction through the provider-approved payment route.
Keep the receipt or transaction evidence and, for prepaid vending, save the electricity token returned after payment.
If payment succeeds but the bill or prepaid units are not reflected, contact YEDC customer care with the account or meter number and transaction evidence.
notes: YEDC says prepaid customers can now buy units online from the company website or at YEDC offices.

Always verify the meter/account number before payment because prepaid units and bill payments are tied to the entered customer record.

title: How to apply for a YEDC prepaid meter under MAP

The customer name, contact phone number, email and service address where the meter is required
The YEDC Business Unit and the number/type of meters required for the premises

steps: Open YEDC's official Request a Meter page and enter the customer account number or application reference.
Choose the intended meter-request action and complete the customer, contact and premises information required by YEDC.
Submit the meter request and allow YEDC to complete the customer KYC and technical/site processing.
Wait for the provider-approved meter payment or deployment instruction rather than paying an unofficial vendor amount.
Keep the application reference and use YEDC's meter request/status route or customer care to follow the application.
notes: YEDC's published MAP form says new customers can be issued Form 74 while existing customers should provide a copy of the bill for the premises.
The current YEDC MAP page does not yet publish live single-phase or three-phase meter prices.
A customer should use the YEDC request route rather than paying a private installer who cannot show an approved MAP instruction.

title: How to apply for a new YEDC electricity connection
summary: YEDC's current new-supply process for prospective customers, beginning with the service application and load assessment and ending with approval, energisation and metering when requirements are satisfied.

feeNote: YEDC does not publish one flat connection fee for every premises. Costs depend on the approved load, equipment and connection requirements; use the official YEDC assessment rather than an unofficial quote.

A completed new-service form containing the terms and conditions for obtaining supply
Access to the premises so YEDC can carry out the load assessment and evaluate the nearest substation capacity
Any service, wiring or equipment requirement identified before YEDC grants final approval
steps: Open YEDC's official Apply for Electricity page and start the online application or submit the formal request through the nearest Business Unit.
Complete the new-service form issued for the prospective customer and provide the premises and load information requested.
Allow YEDC's New Service Officer to assess the premises and compare the expected load with the available capacity of the nearest substation.
Complete any requirement identified during the assessment and wait for the approving authority to grant the connection request.
After approval, confirm energisation and meter installation and keep the new YEDC account information for future billing and support.
notes: YEDC's published process separates ordinary new electricity supply from its Equipment Connection/Modification Request used for customer-owned transformers, feeders, RMUs, poles or cables.

Do not treat the published 24-hour post-approval energisation period as a promise that the entire application process takes 24 hours.

title: How to lodge a complaint with YEDC online

A working phone number and email address for customer contact
The nearest bus stop or landmark for the affected premises or incident
The correct complaint category, subcategory and a clear description of the problem

Choose the complaint category and subcategory that best match the billing, meter, supply or other issue.
Write a concise complaint description with the relevant dates, transaction references or meter details and submit the form.
Save the complaint ID returned by YEDC and use it when following up through official customer-care channels.
notes: YEDC's online form returns a complaint ID after a successful submission.

Keep payment receipts, meter photographs or other evidence when the complaint involves billing or vending.

title: How to recharge a JED prepaid meter online

An accredited JED online vending platform such as one of the examples listed by the company
A payment amount sufficient for the customer's band/tariff, VAT and any applicable third-party platform charge

Enter the recharge amount and review the payment total including any vendor service charge.
Complete payment and save the 20-digit prepaid electricity token returned by the vendor.
Load the token on the meter/UIU and contact JED customer care if a valid token fails or the meter shows a technical error.

If units load as zero, JED says possible causes include a negative balance, failed loading or a meter fault.
